items.bio: I have been working in the mental health field in a variety of settings since 2005. </br></br> My professional and research interests include: promoting resiliency, trauma recovery, Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing (EMDR), anxiety, depression, clinical supervision, and couples counseling. Theories that inform my clinical practice are EMDR, neurocounseling, person-centered, choice theory, mindfulness, Forward Facing Trauma Therapy and CBT. I use Gottman as a foundation for couples work. </br></br> I currently balance my group counseling practice with a clinical supervisor/adjunct teaching appointment in the Department of Counseling at the University of Montana. Additionally, I facilitate resiliency workshops and groups in a variety of settings. </br></br> I can often be found along a mountain trail with her beloved husband, son, daughter and dog.

items.bio: Whether you are navigating a major life transition, managing the daily impacts of anxiety or carrying the heavy weight of trauma, depression, and loneliness I am here to support you. I believe that therapy is a collaborative space where you can show up exactly as you are. Together, we will look at the deeper questions and patterns impacting your life, while actively building the practical tools you need to feel more grounded, resilient, and connected. </br></br> My approach is deeply holistic and tailored to your unique identity and story. I weave evidence-based psychological frameworks with practical mindfulness meditation tools to help you develop sustainable nervous system regulation and self-compassion.Taking the step to begin therapy can feel daunting, but you do not have to navigate these challenges alone. I offer a warm, collaborative, and non-judgmental space where we can work toward the meaningful change and healing you deserve.

items.bio: I'm passionate about helping individuals and families navigate life's challenges with compassion, curiosity, and hope. Grounded in a person-centered, trauma-informed approach, I believe healing begins in relationships where people feel genuinely seen, heard, and accepted. </br></br> My clinical interests include life transitions, relationships, trauma, and parenting. Drawing on my experience as an educator, parent, athlete, and counselor, I bring a practical, relational approach to this work, helping people build healthier relationships and stronger emotional well-being. </br></br> Before becoming a counselor, I spent more than 20 years in public education as a kindergarten teacher and school librarian. Those years deepened my appreciation for the resilience of children, families, and communities, and reinforced how much it matters to create spaces where people feel safe to grow, connect, and thrive. </br></br> I’m drawn to movement and high alpine meadows, coffee, projects, and good stories.

items.bio: Hello! I’m glad you’re here. I work with clients across a wide range of identities, abilities, and life experiences, with a particular interest in supporting older children (ages 8+), adolescents, and adults. I am employed at Julie Ballew, LCPC, LLC as a Professional Counselor Licensure Candidate (PCLC). Julie Ballew, PhD, LCPC, is my licensed supervisor and oversees all of my clinical work. Insurance billing, when applicable, is completed under her name and license.</br></br>A significant part of my work and experience centers on disability, neurodivergence, chronic health conditions, and the many ways these experiences can shape a person’s relationships, identity, sense of belonging, and experience of the world. I especially welcome clients who may not always feel well represented or understood in traditional counseling spaces, including individuals who communicate using augmentative and alternative communication (AAC). I also have considerable training in play therapy, including neurodiversity-affirming approaches, and enjoy working creatively with clients of different ages.</br></br>My approach is collaborative, trauma-informed, and grounded in Adlerian principles. I am interested not only in what is difficult right now, but also in the larger patterns, relationships, experiences, strengths, and meanings that have shaped how you understand yourself and move through the world. Depending on your needs, the counseling process with me may include conversation, reflection, humor, play, art-based activities, metaphor, or other creative ways of making sense of an experience.</br></br>I do not believe counseling needs to feel overly clinical or scripted to be meaningful. My goal is to create a space where you can show up as a whole person—including the complicated, contradictory, unfinished parts—and feel genuinely heard. Together, we can work toward greater understanding, connection, belonging, and ways of living that feel more aligned with who you are.

items.bio: I recently graduated from the University of Montana with a MA in Clinical Mental Health Counseling. I am interested in helping clients navigate life transitions, grief, and trauma in ways that honor their values and strengthen their sense of self. My counseling approach is grounded in Existential-Humanistic Theory and incorporates interventions from Somatic Psychotherapy and Ecotherapy. I happily offer walk-and-talk session to create space to explore not only what’s happening in your mind, but what’s happening in your body and your relationship with the world around you. In addition to individual counseling, I offer couples counseling informed by Imago and Gottman approaches and enjoy facilitating groups focused on happiness and burnout. When I’m not counseling, you can usually find me soaking up Missoula’s beauty—preferably paddle-boarding on a lake!

items.bio: I welcome clients from diverse backgrounds, identities, and lived experiences. Grounded in a Person-Centered Approach, I strive to create an environment where you feel heard, respected, and accepted without judgement. I believe you are the expert on your own life, and my role is to provide a supportive and curious space where you can explore your experiences, discover your strengths, and move toward what feels most authentic and meaningful. </br></br> I value the therapeutic relationship as a space for curiosity, reflection, and growth. I strive to create a space where you can explore the experiences and patterns that have shaped you, recognize the ways you have adapted, and identify opportunities to adjust what may no longer be helpful in the present. Through increased self-awareness and compassion, we can work toward changes that align with your values and goals. </br></br> Outside of the counseling office, I enjoy traveling, discovering new music, and spending time outdoors with my dogs.

items.bio: I am a counselor passionate about helping teens, young adults, couples, and families better understand themselves and their relationships. My approach is warm, curious, and experiential, with a particular interest in the ways past experiences, attachment, and different “parts” of ourselves can shape how we relate, communicate, and respond to one another in the present. </br></br> As a Certified Brainspotting Practitioner, I use Brainspotting and somatic approaches to support deeper trauma work beyond what words alone can sometimes access. I also draw from parts work to help clients approach the overthinking, people-pleasing, striving, shutting down, or protective sides of themselves with greater curiosity and compassion. In my relational work, I'm trained in Imago Relationship Therapy, which helps couples and families slow down patterns of conflict, better understand one another’s experiences, and build greater connection and attunement. </br></br> Outside of work, you can usually find me skiing, seeing live music, experimenting in my garden, or cooking big dinners for friends and family.

items.bio: If you’ve experienced early-life or ongoing trauma, you may notice its effects on how you see yourself and relate to others. I work mainly with women navigating these experiences, using an integrated approach that draws on parts work (IFS-informed), EMDR, and body-based (somatic) techniques. Early sessions focus on understanding your history, the survival strategies your body learned, and how they have helped you feel safe. We then look at whether the ways you cope today are still serving you and supporting the relationships you most want, with others and with yourself. From there, we work together to build a plan at a pace that feels safe for you, one that helps you gain insight, ease out of outdated patterns, and reintroduce yourself to the you that is more resilient, curious, and whole.</br></br>I have been trained in EMDR, with specialty training in a progressive approach which is especially helpful for people living with the effects of long-standing or early-life trauma.
